Form AutoFill settings vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Safari AutoFill and Contacts card fill cover storefront language. iOS settings, the buyer's saved contact card, and App Store Connect actually separate fill behavior from product-page copy:

  • Settings → Safari → AutoFill — Use Contact Info, Credit Cards, and related toggles on the buyer's iPhone or iPad. Controls what Safari and compatible apps can suggest above the keyboard. Does not generate Chinese listing text.
  • AutoFill from Contacts — names, addresses, phone numbers, and email fields pulled from the buyer's My Card or saved contacts. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains one-tap address fill to China storefront readers.
  • AutoFill credit card — saved card numbers and billing details the system can offer at checkout. Your listing may show a card-fill demo; configuring Wallet or PassKit in the binary is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • Keyboard QuickType fill — contact and card suggestions above the key row when the buyer focuses a form field. Listing copy should match what your gallery shows — a contact-fill chip row is not a password vault sheet unless that is what the screenshot depicts.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how well your app supports form AutoFill.

Working form-fill UX in the app and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

What China buyers see when zh-Hans form AutoFill copy is missing

Shoppers and form-heavy app users browsing the China App Store evaluate checkout speed in the first scroll. Common failure modes when only en-US is filled:

  • English title and subtitle — app name and tagline still Latin script while competitors show native Chinese form-fill positioning
  • Untranslated AutoFill badges on screenshots — overlay lines like "AutoFill my details", "One-tap form fill", "AutoFill credit card", or "Safari AutoFill" remain English on zh-Hans gallery frames
  • Checkout value in English — description opens with US form-fill marketing ("Skip typing your address") that China readers skim past or misread
  • Keyword field still en-US — buyers search 自动填充, Safari自动填充, 联系人自动填充, 信用卡自动填充, or 自动填写; an English-only keyword row misses China Search vocabulary

Better zh-Hans listing copy helps checkout-conscious buyers understand form-fill benefits before install. It does not replace Contacts integration, Wallet card setup, or Apple's review decisions.

Common mistakes on form AutoFill zh-Hans listings

  • Assuming Contacts AutoFill localizes automatically — form fill works on device; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US form-fill badges verbatim — Latin "AutoFill credit card" badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Conflating form AutoFill with Passwords vault marketing — description mentions "AutoFill passwords" or "Credential provider extension" when the app actually sells contact-card checkout; see Passwords listing (zh-Hans) for that separate story
  • Conflating form AutoFill with Predictive Text — next-word suggestion bars belong on the Predictive Text guide, not contact-fill marketing
  • Conflating form AutoFill with Passkeys or Sign in with Apple — login badges belong on the Passkeys guide or Sign in with Apple guide
  • Translating the in-app AutoFill sheet only — system UI may show Chinese while the App Store product page stays English
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Expecting AppLocale to wire Contacts or Wallet APIs — CNContactStore, PassKit, and Safari AutoFill entitlements are outside listing rewrite

FAQ

Does turning on Safari AutoFill auto-translate my China listing?

No. Settings → Safari → AutoFill and keyboard AutoFill from Contacts control what the buyer's device fills into forms — they do not create or populate a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback.

What listing fields does AppLocale rewrite for form AutoFill apps?

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines — rewritten from your English form-fill and Safari AutoFill marketing originals.

How is this different from the Passwords and AutoFill listing page?

The Passwords page covers saved-login AutoFill — vault apps, credential provider extensions, AutoFill passwords, and Fill saved logins. This page covers contact info, addresses, credit cards, Safari AutoFill of checkout fields, and AutoFill from Contacts. This page covers AutoFill my details, AutoFill credit card, and Safari form fill. See Predictive Text listing (zh-Hans) if your hero story is typing predictions.

How is this different from Passkeys or Sign in with Apple?

Passkeys marketing covers passwordless FIDO login. Sign in with Apple marketing covers Continue with Apple and Hide My Email. This page covers checkout and registration form AutoFill — not passkey registration and not Apple ID sign-in badges.

Can AppLocale implement Contacts APIs or Wallet card storage?

No. We deliver listing metadata copy only. Contacts framework integration, PassKit card provisioning, Safari AutoFill entitlements, and credential provider engineering are outside AppLocale scope.

Why do screenshot captions still say "AutoFill credit card" in English on China?

Caption and overlay fields are managed per localization. If you filled en-US screenshot text but never saved zh-Hans caption lines — or uploaded the same English-overlay PNGs to the Chinese set — China buyers see Latin form-fill badges on the product page.
